title: IQM Quantum Computers Sells 54-Qubit Radiance R3 System to South Korean Quantum-AI Infrastructure Firm QAI - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX) won an €8–10M order from South Korean data-center operator QAI for an on-premises 54-qubit Radiance R3 superconducting system to be installed in a Seoul private AI data center by end-2027 — IQM's first private commercial data-center deployment in Asia. QAI will pair it with GPU infrastructure and sell Quantum-as-a-Service domestically.

insights.claim: IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX) received an order valued at EUR 8–10 million from South Korean data center and cloud company QAI Co., Ltd. for an on-premises 54-qubit IQM Radiance R3 superconducting quantum computer, due for installation in Seoul by end-2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Implies roughly €150–185k per qubit pricing for on-prem superconducting systems and adds to IQMX backlog; revenue recognition likely ~2027.
insights.locator: IQM Quantum Computers (Nasdaq: IQMX) has received an order

insights.claim: The QAI deal is IQM's first deployment into a private commercial data center in Asia and its second system sale in South Korea, after an IQM Spark installation at Chungbuk National University.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals quantum demand moving from universities/government labs toward commercial data-center operators.

insights.claim: QAI plans to couple the 54-qubit IQM processor with its GPU-based AI infrastructure and offer domestic Quantum-as-a-Service access for drug discovery, battery materials, financial optimization and logistics scheduling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid quantum-GPU data centers are an emerging business model; watch utilization and pricing of national QaaS offerings.

insights.claim: IQM's Radiance R3 uses tunable couplers in a square-lattice topology that natively supports surface-code error correction, pulse-level access and modular component upgrades, designed for low-latency integration with classical HPC clusters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Upgradeable on-prem designs reduce obsolescence risk for buyers — a selling point versus cloud-only competitors.

insights.claim: South Korea's national quantum strategy under the Ministry of Science and ICT targets broad domestic quantum computing utilization by 2035, which the QAI deployment aligns with.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: National sovereignty programs are a key demand driver for on-prem quantum system sales in Asia.
insights.locator: The deployment aligns with South Korea’s national quantum strategy
